title: Yucca House National Monument Expansion Act
official_summary:
Yucca House National Monument Expansion Act

This bill authorizes the Department of the Interior to acquire, by donation, the approximately 160 acres of land and any interests in such land that is identified as the Yucca House National Monument Proposed Boundary Addition.

Upon acquisition of the additional land, Interior shall adjust the boundaries of the monument to include the acquired land.

Such land and any interests in such land shall be administered as part of the monument.

summary.headline: This law lets the federal government accept donated land of about 160 acres to expand Yucca House National Monument in Colorado.
summary.what_it_does: The Department of the Interior is allowed to take ownership of about 160 acres, plus any related interests in that land, if the owners give it to the government as a donation. Once the land is acquired, Interior must change the monument's boundaries to include it. The added land is then managed as part of the monument.

who_it_affects.group: Owners of the proposed addition land
who_it_affects.how: They may choose to donate their land or interests in it to the federal government, but the bill does not require any sale or transfer.

who_it_affects.group: National Park Service and Department of the Interior
who_it_affects.how: They must accept and manage the donated land as part of the monument once it is acquired and the boundaries are adjusted.

who_it_affects.group: Visitors to Yucca House National Monument
who_it_affects.how: If the land is added, the monument's protected area would grow, which could affect how the added land is accessed and used.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The authority took effect when the law was enacted on January 13, 2021, but the boundary change happens only after the land is actually donated and acquired.
